▶ Global AI Optical Transceiver Market to Reach US$26 Billion in 2026; Component Shortages Identified as Primary Capacity Expansion Bottleneck — TrendForce

• TrendForce expects the global AI optical transceiver market to expand from US$16.5 billion in 2025 to US$26 billion in 2026, representing 57% YoY growth.

• This acceleration reflects not only specification upgrades but also a structural reshaping of the optical communications supply chain, driven by the faster pace of AI data center buildouts.

• As AI data center expansion continues, demand for 800G-and-above optical transceivers — used for interconnects between AI server clusters — is surging.

• North American CSP data center traffic is sustaining annual growth of over 30%, with aggressive GPU and AI server deployments by major cloud players driving high growth in high-speed optical interconnects.

• However, constrained production capacity for core optoelectronic chips such as EMLs and CW-LDs is deepening supply shortages, acting as the primary bottleneck for overall optical transceiver capacity expansion.

• In addition, high-precision manufacturing processes such as optical alignment are difficult to scale, and the pace of productivity improvement faces structural limits.

• At the same time, the rising power consumption and heat dissipation challenges of high-speed optical modules are increasing system design complexity, adding pressure on actual data center deployment and mass-production schedules.

• Upstream suppliers, led by NVIDIA and key system vendors, are shifting their procurement strategies — adopting strategic long-term agreements (LTAs) to secure critical components and reduce dependence on short-term spot-market purchases, thereby mitigating supply risk.

• TrendForce emphasizes that growth in the AI optical transceiver market is shifting from a single-product upgrade narrative toward three axes: market expansion, generational technology transitions, and application diversification.

• As 1.6T-generation products gradually enter mass production, demand for edge computing and data center interconnect (DCI) applications is expected to rise, fueling growth in the 800G and 1.6T ZR/ZR+ coherent optical module market.

• In response to component shortages, major international players such as Coherent, Lumentum, and AAOI — along with Taiwanese firms including ELASER and LuxNet Corporation — are moving to expand capacity and adopt new technologies.

• 2026–2027 will be a critical window for establishing positions in the 1.6T supply chain, with success in design-ins at tier-1 customers expected to be the decisive factor for future market share.
